story_title: Antibiotic Resistance Patterns in Bacterial Species
story_subtitle: Analyzing susceptibility to Penicillin, Streptomycin, and Neomycin across bacterial genera and Gram staining categories

story_pieces.narration: Aerobacter aerogenes and Klebsiella pneumoniae exhibit the highest Penicillin resistance (870 μg/mL and 850 μg/mL, respectively), while Bacillus anthracis is highly susceptible (0.001 μg/mL). This highlights significant variation in Penicillin susceptibility among bacterial species.
story_pieces.question: Which bacterial species show the highest and lowest resistance to Penicillin?
story_pieces.visualization: ranked bar chart (bacteria vs. Penicillin MIC values)

story_pieces.narration: Gram-positive bacteria demonstrate consistently higher resistance to all three antibiotics compared to Gram-negative counterparts, with Neomycin resistance in Gram-positive strains averaging 8.59 μg/mL versus 0.59 μg/mL in Gram-negative species. This suggests that Gram staining significantly influences susceptibility patterns.
story_pieces.question: How does Gram staining influence antibiotic susceptibility patterns?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (Gram staining vs. antibiotic resistance values)

story_pieces.narration: The 'other' genus category dominates the dataset (9/16 species), but Salmonella and Streptococcus genera show distinct resistance profiles. Streptococcus species display the highest Neomycin resistance (up to 40 μg/mL), while Salmonella species show moderate Streptomycin resistance (14 μg/mL for S. hemolyticus).
story_pieces.question: Which bacterial genera exhibit unique resistance patterns across antibiotics?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (genus vs. antibiotic resistance averages)

story_pieces.narration: Salmonella species demonstrate exceptional resistance to Streptomycin (14 μg/mL for S. hemolyticus) and Neomycin (40 μg/mL for S. viridans), while Staphylococcus aureus shows minimal resistance to all three antibiotics (0.03 μg/mL for Penicillin and Streptomycin).
story_pieces.question: Which genera have the most extreme resistance profiles?
story_pieces.visualization: clustered bar chart (genus vs. antibiotic resistance extremes)

story_pieces.narration: Streptococcus viridans exhibits the highest Neomycin resistance (40 μg/mL) and shows marked variability in Streptomycin resistance (10 μg/mL), indicating potential genetic diversity within species. This variability may affect treatment strategies.
story_pieces.question: How does resistance variability within genera impact treatment options?
story_pieces.visualization: violin plot (genus vs. Neomycin resistance distribution)
